items.basis: The micro-valve actuation response time versus particle transit time is not adequately addressed. The candidate fails to provide a detailed analysis of the response time, which is critical for effective particle diversion. Without this analysis, it is unclear whether the micro-valve can respond quickly enough to prevent clogging events.

The candidate fails to consider the impact of mill vibration environment on the micro-valve and optical particle sensor. The vibration could cause mechanical stress on the components, leading to premature failure, and also affect the accuracy of the optical particle sensor. This omission undermines the reliability of the proposed solution.

The candidate does not provide any evidence to support the predicted effect of zero clogging events per campaign at full spray uniformity. The absence of any experimental data or simulation results makes it impossible to verify the claim, and the prediction appears to be unfounded.

The candidate fails to demonstrate that the proposed solution can achieve the same or better performance as the baseline system. The predicted effect of zero clogging events per campaign is not sufficient to establish equivalence, as the baseline system may still experience some clogging events. The candidate needs to provide a more comprehensive comparison of the two systems.

The candidate's proposal requires the installation of 120 units of 3 mm in-line micro-valve + optical sorter + micro-ejector assemblies, which could be a significant logistical challenge. The shared 24 V rails along the header may also require additional infrastructure, which could add complexity and cost to the implementation.

The candidate's testable prediction of a single instrumented nozzle assembly passing a 500-hour abrasive-scale slurry challenge with zero throat blockages and flow stability within 2 percent is not clear. The measurement of flow stability within 2 percent is not well-defined, and it is unclear how this measurement will be taken.
